<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2019 Hong Kong protests]]
**[[Hong Kong Police Force|Police]] seal off and trap hundreds of students and protesters inside [[Hong Kong Polytechnic University]] amid fears of a crackdown. After a police officer is injured, security forces threaten to fire live bullets if protesters do not give up lethal weapons. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hong-kong-protests/hong-kong-police-seal-off-university-amid-fears-of-crackdown-idUSKBN1XR0O2 (Reuters)]
**Protesters manage to escape from the university by shimmying down plastic hosing from a bridge and fleeing on waiting motorbikes as the police fire projectiles. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-protests/at-embattled-hong-kong-university-a-dramatic-escape-idUSKBN1XR0O2 (Reuters)]
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]]
**An [[airstrike]] on a biscuit shop kills five [[Bangladesh]]i nationals and two Libyans and wounds 33 others in [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]], [[Libya]]. A U.N. envoy to Libya claims that it could be a [[war crime]]. [https://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/nation/libyan-officials-airstrike-kills-7-workers-in-tripoli-2/ (''The Seattle Times'')]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)]]
**A [[South Korea|South Korean]] oil drilling rig is seized by [[Houthi movement|Houthi rebels]]. It is unknown how many sailors were on board. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/11/yemen-houthi-rebels-seize-vessel-red-sea-191118163426377.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/nov/18/yemens-houthi-rebels-hijack-towboat-with-apparent-saudi-link (The Guardian)]
*[[2019–2020 Iranian protests|2019 Iranian fuel protests]]
**A [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|Revolutionary Guard]] commander vows decisive action to restore calm to [[Iran]]. [https://www.newsweek.com/iran-revolutionary-guards-decisive-action-suppress-deadly-fuel-protests-1472400 (''Newsweek'')]
**The death toll in the protests rises to 12, but reports vary. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-50459971 (BBC News)]
*[[Northern Mali conflict]]
**Militants kill 24 [[Mali Armed Forces|soldiers]] and wound 29 others on an army patrol in northern [[Mali]]. Seventeen militants were also killed in the melee. 6 injured soldiers later die increasing the death toll to 42. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mali-security/mali-army-says-24-soldiers-17-militants-killed-in-attack-on-northern-patrol-idUSKBN1XS2EX (Reuters)] [https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2019/11/19/world/africa/19reuters-mali-security.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Business and economy
*[[Japan]] opens its first military arms show, as it tries to improve its [[military technology]] to combat external threats from [[China]] and [[North Korea]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-japan-defence-exhibition/japan-hosts-first-fully-fledged-arms-show-looking-for-an-edge-in-tech-idUSKBN1XS128?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Fukushima nuclear disaster]]
**The [[Japanese government]] authorizes a release of contaminated water from the plant into the [[Pacific Ocean]]. Officials say that the release represents a "significantly small" risk to human health. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2019/11/69b8ea68fa78-govt-says-safe-to-release-contaminated-fukushima-water-into-ocean.html (Kyodo News Plus)]

;International relations
*[[Russia–Ukraine relations]], [[Ukrainian crisis]]
**[[Russia]] returns three [[Ukrainian Navy]] vessels it seized during [[Kerch Strait incident|an incident]] in the [[Kerch Strait]] last year. [https://www.dw.com/en/russia-returns-navy-vessels-seized-from-ukraine/a-51286196 (Deutsche Welle)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/ukraine-crisis-russia/ukraine-confirms-russia-returning-three-captured-naval-ships-idUSL8N27Y0HU (Reuters)]
*[[Israel–United States relations]], [[Israeli occupation of the West Bank]]
**The [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] announces that the [[United States]] no longer considers [[Israel|Israeli]] settlement of the [[West Bank]] as illegal ''per se'' under international law.  The announcement is praised by Israeli [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]], and condemned by the [[European Union]], the [[Palestinian National Authority]], and [[Jordan|Jordanian]] [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Jordan)|Foreign Affairs Minister]] [[Ayman Safadi]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/nov/18/us-israeli-settlements-no-longer-considered-illegal-palestinian-land-mike-pompeo (''The Guardian'')]

;Law and crime
*[[2019 Hong Kong protests]]
**The [[Hong Kong]] [[High Court (Hong Kong)|High Court]] rules that the [[Government of Hong Kong|government]]'s [[Anti-mask law|mask ban]] violates the [[Hong Kong Basic Law|Basic Law]]. [https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/politics/article/3038184/anti-mask-law-quell-hong-kong-protests-ruled (''South China Morning Post'')] 
*[[LGBT rights in Saudi Arabia]]
**Two [[Saudi people|Saudi]] [[journalist]]s, one of whom worked for [[CNN]] and the [[BBC]], are [[outing|outed]] as [[gay]], which prompts them to flee and seek [[right of asylum|asylum]] in [[Australia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-australia-saudi-asylum/saudi-journalists-who-say-they-were-outed-as-gay-held-in-australian-asylum-center-idUSKBN1XS251 (Reuters)]
*[[2019 Bolivian protests]]
**Interim [[interior minister]] Arturo Murillo threatens to arrest MAS legislators, who refuse to recognize [[Jeanine Áñez]]'s legitimacy, for "subversion". [https://theglobepost.com/2019/11/18/bolivian-government-arrest-mas-lawmakers/ (The Globe Post)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Marshallese general election|Marshall Islands general election]]
**Citizens cast their votes for the 33 members of the country's [[Legislature of the Marshall Islands|legislature]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-marshallislands-election/marshall-islands-heads-to-polls-in-election-closely-watched-by-washington-idUSKBN1XS0F9 (Reuters)]
*[[2019 Bolivian protests]]
**Thousands of Bolivian coca farmers came out in protest in favour of [[Evo Morales]] and called for the resignation of [[Jeanine Áñez|Añez]] as Acting President. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-bolivia-election-idUKKBN1XS29A (Reuters)]
